subject: 1970 Porsche 917 K

taxonomyDecision.construction: mixed transition; generated baseline must use bias/cross-ply compatibility unless direct host/evidence proves otherwise
taxonomyDecision.reason: FIA identifies the 917 as Group 4 and Porsche identifies the 917 K as a 1970 World Sportscar endurance racer; the existing 1968-70 transition class is more specific than generic CLS021/FAM022.

supplier.reason: No source in the focused primary set justifies one supplier across generic 1970 917 K teams and events.

historicalFindings: Porsche describes the 1970 short-tail 917 K as the stabilized evolution used by multiple Porsche-backed teams in the World Sportscar Championship.
The FIA database records Porsche 917 homologation form 250 in Group 4, including 1970 bodywork and 4907 cc extensions.

Porsche records known high-speed tread-separation risk above roughly 350 km/h in the 1970 Le Mans context; this supports preserving a distinct high-speed tire-risk note, not a numeric wear or thermal fit.
Porsche records 343 laps and 4607.811 km for the winning 917 K at Le Mans, but this is vehicle/event endurance context and not evidence that one tire set covered that distance.
